---
title: "API errors and rate limits"
description: "What to do when a BFS API is not available."
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

## The BFS API is not available

If an API is not available, e.g. after too many requests (HTTP 429), a
timeout or a server error, the functions give an error that starts with
"The BFS API is not available.":

```
Error:
! The BFS API is not available.
ℹ HTTP 429 Too Many Requests.
Caused by error in `httr2::req_perform()`:
! HTTP 429 Too Many Requests.
```

Without internet connection, the functions give the message "No internet
connection" and return `NULL`.

## Too many requests

The PXWeb API limits the number of requests per IP address in a time window
(see its [configuration](https://www.pxweb.bfs.admin.ch/api/v1/de/?config)).
`bfs_get_data()` sends two requests: one for the variables of the dataset,
one for the data. If you call it in a loop:

- wait between the calls, e.g. with `delay = 10` (seconds) or
  `Sys.sleep()`,
- save the results rather than downloading them again.

If the error remains, the dataset may be too large for the API. Download
only part of it with `query` (see
[Data catalog and PXWeb datasets](pxweb.html)), or the whole PX file with
`bfs_download_asset()` (see [Tables and files](tables-and-files.html)).

## Handle the errors in your code

The errors have the class `bfs_http_error`, so you can handle them, e.g. to
retry later or skip a dataset:

```r
data <- tryCatch(
  bfs_get_data(number_bfs = "px-x-1502040100_131", language = "en"),
  bfs_http_error = function(e) {
    message("Skipped: ", conditionMessage(e))
    NULL
  }
)
```

The original error classes and fields are kept, e.g. `httr2_http_429` with
the response in `e$resp`, or `http_429` for the errors of pxweb:

```r
tryCatch(
  bfs_get_sse_metadata("DF_LWZ_1"),
  httr2_http_429 = function(e) httr2::resp_retry_after(e$resp)
)
```

The original error is also in `e$parent`.

## Caches

The base maps of `bfs_get_base_maps()` are cached on disk, and the list of
the Swiss Stats Explorer datasets for the R session. If a base map or a new
dataset seems missing, clear the cache with `bfs_clear_cache()`.
